- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive and recent highs are sustained; reduce forecast peak values if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or shows strong downward momentum; adjust downward bias by 5–10% if sentiment < 0.5.
- Lagged forecasts tend to overreact to recent sentiment spikes; apply a 1–2 day smoothing filter to reduce overshoot after sharp sentiment upturns.
- Mean reversion is stronger in early 30-day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 3–5% unless sentiment is strong and rising.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes (especially >0.8) should be capped at +5% above the 14-day moving average to prevent overcorrection.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive values < 0.4), reduce forecast by 2–4% to account for risk aversion.
- Forecast should not exceed 15% above the 30-day moving average unless sentiment is >0.8 and trending upward.
